synthetic_verdict_rule.rule: u = int(sha256('synthetic-verdict-v2:{seed}:{candidate_id}')[:12], 16) / 16**12; hit if u < 0.25, hold if u < 0.28, else miss. Queue items are blinded (no label_iou), so the hash rule was used for every candidate. Missing-candidate hits get unique_error_id M1, M2, ... per image.
synthetic_verdict_rule.first_attempt_discarded: The first run hashed '{seed}:{candidate_id}' with seed 1, which is exactly the D9 tie key sha256('{tie_seed}:{candidate_id}') with tie_seed=1. Among the 90 tied IoU-0 labels the smallest tie keys are the smallest hashes, so all 20 all_label_iou top-N were synthetic hits (difference 14 [4, 15]). Artifact of the synthetic rule, not of the pipeline; rerun with a salted hash. Lesson for any future synthetic check: never derive synthetic verdicts from sha256('{tie_seed}:{id}').

missing_preregistered_query.consequence: The D7 step-1 missing-layer query as written in the preregistration cannot run on this ruler. The user decision (a) 'unmatched_objectlab: report as not measurable' needs either a query without unmatched_objectlab or an export mode that reports an empty population; which one is a user/prereg decision, not changed here.
